_comment: SUPPLIER MAP (wp_suppliers.build): evidence pattern -> the SaaS / infrastructure SUPPLIER a subject organisation uses, with a category. Feeds cases/<id>/suppliers.json (contract C3) for the third-party-risk step in techniques/fx-supplier-exposure.md. A supplier is a RELATIONSHIP OF THE SUBJECT, never an operator link: thousands of unrelated customers share every row below, so nothing here may ever become a KB edge or a cluster key. Mail exchangers are NOT listed here — they reuse mail_providers.json -> mx_providers through wp_recon._classify_mx, and an SPF include matching no row below falls back to that same table, so add a mail provider there, not here. Matching is case-insensitive. Add a row when a token/host shows up unclassified in a run; check the vendor's own documentation for the exact record shape first.

txt_tokens._comment: Apex TXT record PREFIX (lowercase, matched at the start of the record) -> {supplier, category}. Each prefix is a vendor's domain-verification record: the subject proved control of the domain to that vendor, so the vendor holds an account for it. A dormant record may outlive the account (stale).

spf_includes._comment: SPF include: host -> {supplier, category}. A signature beginning with '.' matches as a SUFFIX; '~' as a SUBSTRING (use it for hosts that start with '_', e.g. '~_spf.example-vendor.com', because the reference loader treats any key beginning with '_' as documentation and drops it); otherwise the host matches exactly or as a parent domain. An include matching nothing here falls back to mail_providers.json mx_providers (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Zoho ...), so those are deliberately absent. An include authorises the vendor to SEND as the subject — a phishing-relevant trust.

cname_probe_labels._comment: Subdomain labels whose CNAME chain the collector resolves only when collecting an APEX in an organisation case (scope.json subject_type=org, read via WP_CASE_DIR; wp_recon.detect_cnames -> artifacts.cnames). The apex itself is rarely a CNAME; vendor-served names usually sit on these labels. Every actual collected host, including www, still gets its own chain regardless of scope. Missing, unreadable or non-organisation scope means no guessed-label probes. Queries go through the recursive resolver, but cache misses and guessed labels are visible to the target's authoritative NS — not invisible passive collection; no web/TLS connection is made to the target.

cname_limits._comment: CNAME resolution bounds: max_hops stops a looping chain; timeout is seconds per dig/nslookup query.

cname_targets._comment: CNAME target host -> {supplier, category}. '.'-prefixed = suffix match, else exact or parent domain. A subject subdomain aliased onto a vendor host means the vendor serves that name (and a CNAME left pointing at a cancelled account is a takeover risk worth noting).

ns_hosts._comment: Authoritative nameserver host -> {supplier, category}. '.'-prefixed = suffix match; '~'-prefixed = substring (for providers whose NS hosts sit on many registrable domains, e.g. awsdns-NN); otherwise exact or parent domain.

cert_issuers._comment: Lowercase SUBSTRING of a certificate's issuer string -> {supplier, category}. Only the subject's own hosts count; a CDN often obtains the certificate on the subject's behalf, so this is medium confidence at most.

document_keywords._comment: Whole-word keyword (lowercase) found in a hosted document's metadata (producer / creator tool / software / title) -> {supplier, category}. A mention only says the tool touched one file; it never proves an account, so it is always LOW confidence.

confidence._comment: Evidence kind -> confidence when seen on the subject's OWN apex ('apex') vs one of its subdomains ('subdomain'). A supplier takes the highest confidence across its evidence. 'document' is always low.

caveats._comment: Fixed caveat lines written into every suppliers.json so the reader of the file alone sees the limits.
values: A supplier is a third-party relationship of the subject, never an operator link or an attribution edge.
A shared SaaS vendor does not mean compromise; a vendor breach is a risk to the subject only where the subject's data or access was in scope.
A dormant verification TXT record may outlive the account it verified (stale); corroborate with MX, SPF or a live login page before asserting current use.
A document mention shows one file passed through a tool; it does not prove an account (low confidence).
